## Highlights

Labradorite 1.5 adds more Markdown syntax, richer editing in Write, and quicker
navigation while keeping notes as plain files in the same vault format.

## Writing and rendering

- **Formulas and Mermaid diagrams in Write:** rendered locally, with their
  source editable below the result and a live rendering. Apply or Ctrl/⌘ Enter
  saves, Escape cancels, and undo restores the previous source. Renderers load
  only for notes that need them; diagrams block images, URLs, configuration and
  custom styling directives.
- **Footnotes and callouts:** edit numbered, named and inline footnotes in
  Write. Callouts render with editable type, title, body and folding controls.
- **More syntax:** highlights and six highlight colours, hidden `%%comments%%`,
  custom task statuses, links to headings and blocks, and image sizes.
- **Preview:** note, section and block embeds with depth, cycle and total-size
  limits; a sanitised allowlist for HTML formatting.
- **Properties:** typed fields for simple YAML values, with raw editing for
  richer YAML and TOML front matter.
- **Markdown editing:** heading and list folding, multiple cursors, rectangular
  selections and selecting the next match.

## Source preservation

Opening a note in Write or switching views does not save it. After an edit,
untouched blocks and their separators are saved as written. Supported details
inside edited blocks retain escapes, character references, emphasis delimiters,
list markers, code fences, line breaks and unchanged table rows. Formulas,
diagrams and footnote sources retain their original syntax.

Write uses Markdown view when it cannot safely round-trip syntax, including raw
HTML, note embeds, reference-style link definitions and some complex layouts.
Editing a table row can compact that row's padding; Markdown view remains
available for whitespace-sensitive edits.

## Navigation and appearance

- A persistent icon rail keeps notes, search, recent notes, creation, commands
  and settings reachable when the notes panel is closed. Shortcuts can be
  reordered with dragging or the keyboard.
- Pins, recent notes, clickable folder breadcrumbs, visited-note navigation
  and remembered folder/pin collapse choices make notes easier to revisit.
- The title and document menus sit over the writing area, with a separate
  formatting panel for Write and compact controls on phones.
- Click a title to rename or move the note in place. The field currently
  contains the full path, with the note name selected.
- The theme list has Light and Dark filters, search and keyboard previews.
  The selected filter is remembered; the confirmation shows the theme name.

## Reliability and security

- Renamed note addresses remain valid through refreshes, and moved notes keep
  relative image links pointing at the same files.
- Draft migration keeps the original until its copy is safely stored and
  distinguishes the default vault from explicitly selected vaults.
- A late image upload cannot insert into a different note opened meanwhile.
- The phone notes drawer keeps keyboard focus out of the covered document.
- Builds use Go 1.26.10; CI scans Go vulnerabilities, checks bundled assets
  and runs browser regression tests. Release workflows use pinned actions and
  publish with restricted permissions.

Labradorite is intended for a computer used by one person. Its local API
protections address unrelated web pages; they do not isolate notes from other
accounts or programs on the same computer.

## Upgrading and remaining work

Stop Labradorite, replace the binary and restart it. No vault conversion is
needed from 1.0; notes, themes, trash, history, attachments and browser drafts
carry over. Keep backups of important notes.

Custom task statuses still differ visually between Write and Preview. Editing
only the leaf title inline and an interface rethink are tracked for 2.0; the
interface work starts with a separate brainstorm.

The download is one **Linux amd64** archive with the binary, guide, license and
third-party notices. Verify it against `SHA256SUMS`.

[Full changelog: v1.0.0 → v1.5.0](https://github.com/eg36/Labradorite/compare/v1.0.0...v1.5.0)
